newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus accuses Turkey of violating its airspace.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus accuses Turkey of violating its airspace.

text.p: The Cyprus government said three Turkish F-4 warplanes violated its airspace on Tuesday and it would protest to the United Nations.
The incident comes a month before long-awaited talks between the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities on how to reunite the island, divided after a Turkish invasion in 1974.

"Three Turkish F-4 airplanes today violated the airspace of Cyprus...Turkey has chosen the path of provocations and violations of international world order. Its illegal actions will be reported to the United Nations and other international organisations," government spokesman Manolis Christofides told reporters.
Turkish authorities were unavailable for comment.

However, Christofides said the Greek Cypriot-led government would not reverse its decision to suspend Greek military flights over the divided island. The flights were carried out under a defence pact between the governments of Greece and Cyprus. The Greek Cypriots do not have an airforce.

Two months ago the Greek Cypriot-led government announced it was suspending Greek military flights over the divided island in order to facilitate a U.N. dialogue to prepare the direct talks expected to start on July 9.
Greek Cypriot defence sources told Reuters that since then, Turkish flights over the island have been "sporadic" rather than frequent.

"The decision of the Cyprus government to suspend Greek military flights over Cyprus is still valid in view of the direct talks and in the framework of the declared position that there should be goodwill and a good atmosphere at these talks," said Christofides.

President Glafcos Clerides, as Greek Cypriot leader, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash, who heads a Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in northern Cyprus recognised only by Ankara, are to meet in New York in their first face-to-face encounter for nearly three years.
Some 30,000 Turkish troops are stationed in northern Cyprus, occupied in 1974 in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
